page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288 is a compute-focused server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 288 virtual CPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 1080.0 GB of dedicated RAM, yielding 3.75 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix mathematics. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving 1062.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22997.34 GB/sec for cached small-block reads. The instance also demonstrates strong database capabilities, processing 406.06 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50% of tested hardware.

While the instance excels at parallel processing, software compilation, and prompt processing for large language models, its text generation speeds for small models are relatively weak, falling in the bottom 25%. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-intensive workloads. Given its massive core count and high memory bandwidth, the c4-standard-288 is highly cost-efficient for dense compute workloads, multi-threaded simulation, large-scale web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288 is a high-density compute instance featuring 288 vCPUs and 1080 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers top-tier multi-core performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, exceeding 1000 GB/sec for uncached reads. The processor integrates Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, making it highly capable for vector and matrix computations. While single-core performance is average and the instance lacks local storage or GPUs, its massive parallel processing capacity excels in multi-threaded workloads. It is highly suited for software compilation, database operations, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
